CAN THE ISLANDS BE DEFENDED WITHOUT UNITED STATES HELP? NO. 

IF THE CHINESE REDS HIT MATSU WITH EVERYTHING THEY HAVE, THE 
NATIONALIST CHINESE COULD PROBABLY HOLD OUT 10 DAYS TO TWO’ WEEKS. 
THEN THEIR NAVY AND AIR FORCE WOULD NEED REPLACEMENTS AND NONE ARE 
AVAILABLE. THE UNITED STATES NAVY, AND ULTIMATELY THE AIR FORCE, 
FLYING FROM EITHER FORMOSA OR OKINAWA, WOULD HAVE TO ASSUME 
RESPONSIBILITY FOR THE ISLANDS. 

WHAT WOULD HAPPEN IF WE SURRENDERED THE ISLANDS WITHOUT A FIGHT? 
THE REMAINING COUNTRIES OF ASIA WOULD BE TEMPTED TO JOIN THE COMMUNIST 
PARADE; THE EFFECT ON FORMOSA WOULD BE CATASTROPHIC; THE EFFECT ON 
JAPAN WOULD BE DANGEROUS. I AM CONVINCED THAT THE EFFECT UPON THE 
UNITED STATFS WOULD BE PROFOUND AND DISASTROUS.

WASHINGTON, MARCH 8 CAP)-COMMUNISTS ARE PLOTTING TO “HAMSTRING® ~ 
THE FBI'S INFORMANT SYSTEM, ASSTe ATTYs-GENe WILLIAM Fe TOMPKINS TOLD 
“ONGRESS TODAY. 

®IT 1S BECOMING INCREASINGLY CLEAR,*® HE REPORTED TO A SENATE 
SOVERNMENT OPERATIONS SUBCOMMITTEE, "THAT THE CURRENT ATTACK AGAINST 
“OVERNMENT WITNESSES AND INFORMANTS OF THE FBI HAS ITS ROOTS IN A 
“OMMUNIST EFFORTe™ 

THE JUSTICE DEPARTMENT HAS BEEN UNDER CRITICISM ON THE GROUND THAT 
SOME OF ITS WITNESSES HAVE BEEN UNRELIABLE. CRITICS HAVE POINTED 
FSPECIALLY TO HARVEY MATUSOW, A KEY GOVERNMENT WITNESS IN A STRING OF

NAGY, A RUSSIAN-TRAINED, OLDTIME COMMUNIST REVOLUTIONARY, SERVED 
AS ONE OF HUNGARY'S FIVE VICE PREMIERS BEFORE STEPPING UP TO THE 
PREMIERSHIP. HE HAD FOUGHT IN RUSSIA AT THE OUTBREAK OF THE 1917 RED 
REVOLUTION, WORKING BETWEEN THE WARS IN THE HUNGARIAN COMMUNIST PARTY, 
AND DURING WORLD WAR II WENT BACK TO RUSSIA AS A HUNGARIAN LANGUAGE 
BROADCASTER. 

RETURNING TO HIS HOMELAND WITH THE RED ARMY IN 1944, HE ROSE RAPID- 
LY IN THE NEW HUNGARIAN COMMUNIST HIERARCHY. HE BECAME SUCCESSIVELY 
AGRICULTURE MINISTER, INTERIOR MINISTER--A KEY POST WITH FAR FLUNG AU- 
THORITY OVER INTERNAL SECURITY--AND PARLIAMENT SPEAKER BEFORE BEING 
NAMED A VICE PREMIER. 

RAKOSI, A BULLET-HEADED MAN OF 63, HAS HAD A LONG, BRILLIANT AND 
OFTEN VIOLENT CAREER IN INTERNATIONAL COMMUNISM. AT 28 HE WAS SECRE- 
TARY OF THE COMINTERN EXECUTIVE, WHICH DIRECTED COMMUNIST ACTIVITIES 
OUTSIDE THE SOVIET UNION BEFORE WORLD WAR II. 

RETURNING TO HUNGARY IN THE PERIOD BETWEEN THE TWO WORLD WARS TO AID 
THE COMMUNIST CAUSE THERE, HE SERVED SEVERAL LONG PRISON TERMS 
ON CHARGES OF MURDER AND INCITING TO MURDER. 

LIKE NAGY. RAKOSI WAS IN RUSSIA DURING WORLD WAR II AND RETURNED 


HOME WITH THE ADVANCING SOVIET ARMIES. LONG CONSIDERED STALIN'S 
HATCHETMAN IN HUNGARY, HE HAS BEEN THE REAL POWER IN HUNGARY SINCE |. 
1945. HE WAS ONE OF THE FEW HIGH-PLACED JEWS IN THE RED WORLD TO RETA 
HIS POST DURING THE ANTI©SEMITIC WAVE THAT MARKED STALIN'S LAST MONTHSs 

RAKOSI ONCE DESCRIBED HIS "SALAMI TACTICS" OF PUSHING COMMUNIS? 
CONTROL OVER THE COUNTRY AS: “DEMANDING A LITTLE MORE EACH DAY, LIKE 
CUTTING UP A SALAMI, THIN SLICE AFTER THIN SLICE. :

OF HEAVY INDUSTRY.“ THAT MEANS A RETURN TO THE STALINIST PROGRAM

BY BRACK CURRY (210) 

BONN, GERMANY, MARCH $ (AP)=THE NATIONAL COMMITTEE OF THE FREE 
DEMOCRATIC PARTY (FDP) TONIGHT CALLED FOR FDP TO SAY IN THE COALITION 
GOVERNMENT. BUT IT SOLIDLY SUPPORTED THE PARTY'S DEFIANCE OF 
CHANCELLOR KONRAD ADENAUVER-ON THE SAAR -ESSUE.~ - 

THE COMMITTEE APPROVED THE RESIGNATION OF VICE CHANCELLOR FRANZ 
BLUECHER, FDP MEMBER WHO RESIGNED FROM THE GOVERNMENT AFTER VOTING 
FOR THE FRENCH-GERMAN AGREEMENT TO “EUROPEANIZE" THE SAAR, IN OP- 
POSITION TO HIS PARTY'S OFFICIAL STAND. ADENAUER HAS NOT YET 
ACCEPTED THE RESIGNATION. 

THESE DECISIONS AT AN EXTRAORDINARY ALL-DAY MEETING OF THE 80- 
MEMBER COMMITTEE TOSSED INTO ADENAUER'S LAP THE FUTURE OF HIS FOUR- 
PARTY COALITION. 

FORTY OF THE 47 FDP DEPUTIES IN THE BUNDESTAG (LOWER HOUSE) VOTED 
AGAINST THE SAAR SETTLEMENT IN THE RATIFICATION VOTE ON THE PARIS 
TREATIES, DESPITE A THREAT BY ADENAUER TO EXPEL THE PARTY FROM HIS 
GOVERNMENT. 

TONIGHT THE NATIONAL COMMITTEE ANNOUNCED ITS APPROVAL OF "THE 
CLEAR POSITION OF THE FDP DEPUTIES IN THE VOTES ON THE SAAR . 
AGREEMENT AND THE ATTITUDE OF FDP DEPUTY MAX BECKER AND FDP NATIONAL 
CHAIRMAN THOMAS DEHLER." 

DURING THE PARLIAMENTARY DEBATE ON THE PARIS TREATIES, BECKER 
ASSAILED THE SAAR AGREEMENT AS A GIVEAWAY OF GERMAN TERRITORY. DEHLER

NIGHT LEAD ARABS (180) 

DAMASCUS, SYRIA, MARCH 10 CAP)-SYRIA, EGYPT AND SAUDI ARABIA-- 
PUSHING THELR PROPOSED ARAB DEFENSE ORGANIZATION--HAVE AGREED THAT AN 
EGYPTIAN WOULD HEAD A UNIFIED COMMAND WITH HEADQUARTERS HERE, 
INFORMED SOURCES SAID TODAY. : 

THE DECISION WAS REGARDED AS AN IMPORTANT VICTORY IN SUPPORT OF 
EGYPT'S CLAIM TO LEADERSHIP OF THE MIDDLE EAST ARAB WORLD AND A TRIBUTE 
AS WELL TO SYRIA. 

EARLIER TODAY, SYRIAN FOREIGN MINISTER KHALED EL AZEM TOLD NEWSMEN 
THE UNIFIED COMMAND WOULD HAVE FULL AUTHORITY OVER MEMBER STATES AND 
THEIR ARMIES ONLY IN WARTIME. IN PEACE ONLY PARTS OF THE ARMIES 
WOULD BE UNDER THE COMMANDER, HE SAID. 

EL AZEM ALSO SAID THE PROPOSED ORGANIZATION, WHICH HAS BARRED 
IRAQ BECAUSE IT SIGNED A DEFENSE PACT WITH NON-ARAB TURKEY, WOULD 
CERTAINLY GO TO IRAQ'S RESCUE IF IRAQ IS ATTACKED. HE ADDED HE WILL 
VISIT BAGHDAD MONDAY TO "KEEP STRONG AND FRIENDLY RELATIONS 
BETWEEN IRAQ AND MEMBERS OF THE NEW DEFENSE ORGANIZATION.® 

HE EMPHASIZED THE NEW GROUPING WILL NOT BE CONFINED TO THE THREE 
COUNTRIES FORMING IT BUT ALSO WILL BE OPEN TO ALL ARAB STATES WITH 
ARMIES UNDER NATIONAL COMMAND. AZEM SAID JORDAN WOULD BE ADMITTED 
IF IT GETS RID OF BRITISH OFFICERS IN ITS ARAB LEGION AND FREES 
ITSELF OF OBLIGATIONS TO BRITAIN UNDER THE 1948 TREATY. BRITAIN 
SUPPORTS THE ARAB LEGION WITH A SUBSIDY PAID ANNUALLY.

NIGHT LEAD VIET NAM (290) 


BY JOHN RODERICK 

SAIGON, INDOCHINA, MARCH 10 (AP)-INTERNAL DIFFICULTIES ARE 
SERIOUSLY SHAKING THE POSITION OF NATIONALIST PREMIER NGO DINH DIEM, 
THE MAN PRESIDENT EISENHOWER AND SECRETARY OF STATE DULLES CONSIDER 
MOST LIKELY TO SAVE SOUTH VIET NAM FROM COMMUNISM. 

DIEM'S ENEMIES--THE CAO DAI AND HOA HAO RELIGIOUS SECTS 
THE BINH XUYEN SOCIETY AND THE DAI VIET POLITICAL PARTY--HAVE 
UNDERTAKEN A CONCERTED CAMPAIGN TO UNSEAT HIM. THEY ARE ASSAILING HIM 
ON BOTH MILITARILY AND POLITICALLY. 

THE STRUGGLE WHICH IS LOOMING BETWEEN THE GOVERNMENT AND ITs 
ADVERSARIES THREATENS TO PARALYZE THE SOUTH FOR MONTHS. 

THE SITUATION IS DANGEROUS BECAUSE ALL FOUR OF PREMIER DIEM'S

ARRANGED. 

RUSSIAN STUDENT EDITORS WHO HAVE BEEN GRANTED PERMISSION TO

MORE THAN “21. aR a

RUSSIANS ARE REALLY GRADUATE STUDENTS, EDITORS OF STUDENT PUBLICATIONS.

HAS BEEN SEIZED ON BY RUSSIAN PROPAGANDISTS AS GROUNDS FOR CRITICISM 
OF THE UNITED STATES. 

SUYDAM SAID THE GROUP'S ITINERARY WOULD BE WORKED OUT WITH THE HELP 
OF THE INSTITUTE OF INTERNATIONAL EDUCATION, OF NEW YORK. HE SAID THE 
STATE DEPARTMENT HAD ASKED THIS PRIVATE ORGANIZATION TO MAKE THE 
NECESSARY ARRANGEMENTS DIRECTLY WITH THE EDITORS AND THE SOVIET GOVERN- 
MENT.

IN NEVADA MONDAY. BY TOMORROW NIGHT, THE BUREAU SAID, IT WILL HAVE

THE SENATE VOTE COMPLETED ITALIAN PARLIAMENTARY ACTION ON THE 
ACCORDS. IT MADE ITALY THE EIGHTH OF THE 15 NATIONS INVOLVED TO CoM- 
PLETE SUCH ACTION. ITALY'S LOWER HOUSE, THE CHAMBER OF DEPUTIES, AP- 
OROVED THE TREATIES DEC. 23 BY 335-215. 

IN ADDITION TO PROVIDING FOR GERMAN TROOPS AS PART OF THE WESTERN 
LINEUP AGAINST THE THREAT OF RED AGGRESSION, THE ACCORDS PROVIDE FOR 
RESTORATION OF WEST GERMAN SOVEREIGNTY AND FOR ADMISSION OF WEST 
SERMANY INTO THE NORTH ATLANTIC TREATY ORGANIZATION (NATO). 

THE VOTE CAME AFTER TWO WEEKS OF SENATE DEBATE THAT SAW FIST FIGHTS 
BREAK OUT ON THE FLOOR OF THE CHAMBER. THERE ALSO WERE NOISY DIS- 
JRDERS ON THE STREETS OF ROME. 

THE COMMUNISTS HAVE BITTERLY OPPOSED WESTERN UNION AND FOUGHT 
RATIFICATION OF THE ACCORDS HERE TO THE END. POLICE AND COMMUNIST 
DEMONSTRATORS CLASHED BRIEFLY OUTSIDE THE SENATE WHILE THE VOTE WAS 
3EING TAKEN. 

ABOUT 1,000 POLICE RINGED THE SENATE BUILDING DURING THE FINAL 
JOURS OF THE SENATE SESSION. THEY BLOCKED ALL STREETS LEADING TO THE 
3U ILDING. 

AT ONE POINT POLICE CHARGED A GROUP OF SHOUTING COMMUNIST 
DEMONSTRATORS AND SENT THEM SCURRYING DOWN SIDE STREETS. SEVERAL 
DEMONSTRATORS WERE TAKEN INTO CUSTODY, BRINGING THE NUMBER OF ARRESTS 
IN TWO DAYS OF RIOTING AND DEMONSTRATIONS TO MORE THAN 50. 

IN ONE SECTOR POLICE CHARGED INTO A GROUP OF WILDLY SHOUTING 
RED DEMONSTRATORS AND SENT THEM SCURRYING DOWN SIDE STREETS. ONE MAN 
WAS INJURED. IN THIS MELEE AND OTHER DEMONSTRATIONS OVER THE CITY 
POLICE PICKED UP MORE THAN 500 PERSONS TONIGHT BUT RELEASED 
MOST OF THEM. 

AS A LAST MINUTE PROTEST AGAINST RATIFICATION OF THE PACTS AND 
AGAINST AN ATTACK WEDNESDAY ON COMMUNIST PARTY HEADQUARTERS HERE, THE 
REN-ROSSED ROME CHAMBER OF LABOR CALLED MUT ITS MEMBERS IN A TWO2HOUR 

GENERAL STRIKE TODAY. THE STRIKE HAD LITTLE EFFECT, SINCE NON- 
COMMUNIST UNIONS HAD INSTRUCTED THEIR MEMBERS TO STAY ON THE JOB. 

IN PUSHING THE APPROVAL THROUGH THE SENATE THE GOVERNMENT HAD THE 
SOLID BACKING OF THE FOUR-PARTY CENTER COALITION--THE CHRISTIAN 
DEMCCRATS, SOCIAL DEMOCRATS, LIBERALS AND REPUBLICANS~-AND THE SUPPORT 
OF THE MONARCHISTS AND MEMBERS OF THE FASCIST ITALIAN SOCIAL MOVE-

~” SAIGON, INDOCHINA, MARCH 13 CAP)-MENACED IN THE NORTH BY ARMED

AND PRIVATE INTERESTS, PREMIER NGO DINH DIEM TODAY FACES ONE OF HIS 
MOST SERIOUS CRISES. 

MORE THAN EIGHT MONTHS AFTER COMING TO POWER THE GOVERNMENT CONTROLS 
LESS THAN HALF OF THE SOUTH VIET NAM. 

THE DALVIET POLITICAL PARTY, THE HOA HAO AND CAO DAI RELIGIOUS 
SECTS AND THE BINH XUYEN ORGANIZATION OF FORMER RIVER™PIRATES ARF 
PREVENTING THE PREMIER FROM PLANTING THE RED STRIPED YELLOW NATIONAL 
FLAG IN THE REMAINDER OF THE NON-COMMUNIST TERRITORY.- 

DIEM HAS RESORTED TO FORCE AGAINST THE DAI VIET, WHO RALLIED ABOUT 
1,9 DESERTERS FROM THE NATIONAL GUARD TO THEIR SIDE, CLOSE TO THE 
197TH PARALLEL, THE DIVIDING LINE BETWEEN NORTH AND SOUTH VIET NAMs NINE 
BATTALIONS SUPPORTED BY TANKS AND ARTILLERY HAVE LAUNCHED A CAMPAIGN 
AGAINST THEIR STRONGHOLD AT BALANG, 2O MILES WEST OF QUANGTRI, AND 
HAVE SUCCEEDED IN TAKING THEIR ABANDONED HEADQUARTERS. BUT THE BULK OF 
THE DESERTERS ESCAPED THE NATIONALIST NET DESPITE THE SURRENDER OF ABOUT 
100 OF THEM YESTERDAY. 

THE BIG MILITARY ACTION IN THE NORTH HAS TIED THE HANDS OF THE 





SOVERNMENT IN THE SOUTH, WHERE 12 BATTALIONS ARE IMMOBILIZED IN THE 
“AMAU REGION AND OTHERS ARE BEING HARRIED BY THE FORCES OF ONE-ARMED 


QUANG VINH, OF THE HOA HAO.

BETTER KNOWN AS BACUT, WILL BE A LAST RESORT IF ALL OTHER METHODS FAIL.

NEW PARTNERS IN A UNITED SPECIAL INTEREST FRONT--GEN,TRAN VAN SOAI OF

CONTROLS SAIGON'S POLICE AND ALSO MOST OF ITS UNDERWORLD. 

ONE OF THE REASONS FOR THE PRESENT CRLTICAL TURN OF EVENTS WAS

TO PUBLIC HEALTH IN COLORADO. | | 
HOWEVER, THE SCIENTISTS RESTATED THEIR POSITION AFTER CONFERRING WITH 
WARD DARLEY, CU PRESIDENT, AND DRe LEO SZILARD, FAMED BIOPHYSICIST 


THE UNIVERSITY OF CHICAGO. | 
THE SCIENTISTS--DRSe RAY Re LANIER, HEAD OF THE CU MEDICAL 
SCHOOL'S RADIOLOGY DEPARTMENT, AND THEODORE PUCK, CHIEF OF THE BIO- 
SHYSICS DEPARTMENT--TOUCHED OFF A FUROR AMONG STATE AND GOVERNMENT OFFI-

WASHINGTON,MARCH 15 (AP)-SECRETARY OF STATE DULLES SAID TODAY THE 
UNITED STATES HOPES TO HAVE NEW PROPOSALS TO STABILIZE THE NEAR EAST, 
NOW BITTERLY DIVIDED BETWEEN ISRAEL AND THE ARAB STATES. 

BUT THE SECRETARY SAID TO A NEWS CONFERENCE THAT INCIDENTS HAVE KEPT 
OCCURRING WHICH MADE IT DIFFICULT FOR THIS COUNTRY TO PERFECT ITS 
PLANS FOR THE REGION. 

THIS WAS APPARENTLY A REFERENCE, AMONG OTHER THINGS, TO THE 
VIOLENT CLASH EARLY THIS MONTH BETWEEN ISRAELI AND EGYPTIANS IN THE 
GAZA ‘ 

THE FIGHTING IN WHICH MORE THAN 30 EGYPTIANS WERE KILLED HAS BEEN 
BLAMED ON ISRAEL BY ARMISTICE OBSERVERS IN THE AREA. 
SECURITY COUNCIL IS PREPARING TO REVIEW THE CASE.

INTERMITTENTLY FOR SIX MONTHS WITH THE ISRAELI AMBASSADOR TO WASHING- 
TON, ABBA EBANe

ARRANGEMENTS ISRAEL ALSO SHOULD BE GIVEN WEAPONS TO KEEP FROM BEING PUT 
AT A MILITARY DISADVANTAGEs

WASHINGTON, MARCH.16 (AP)-THE LONG SECRET RECORDS OF THE YALTA\? ~° 
CONFERENCE IN 1945 WERE MADE PUBLIC TONIGHT. 

THEY DISCLOSED, AMONG OTHER THINGS, THAT SOVIET MARSHAL JOSEPH 
STALIN DEMANDED SWEEPING CONCESSIONS FROM PRESIDENT ROOSEVELT IN THE 
FAR EAST WITH THE ARGUMENT THAT HE HAD “TO EXPLAIN TO THE SOVIET PEOPLE 
WHY RUSSIA WAS ENTERING THE WAR AGAINST JAPAN." 

THE CONCESSIONS WHICH HE SPECIFIED INCLUDED POSSESSION OF THE KURILE 
ISLANDS AND SOUTHERN SAKHALIN, RIGHTS TO THE PORT OF DAIREN AND PORT 
ARTHUR AND OPERATION OF THE CHINESE EASTERN AND SOUTH MANCHURIAN 


RAILROADS.» | ! : 
ROOSEVELT, ANXIOUS TO ASSURE RUSSIA'S BELLIGERENCY IN THE FAR 


EAST, AGREED TO THE CONCESSIONS.» 
CRITICS OVER THE YEARS HAVE ACCUSED HIM OF BLUNDERING, OR WORSE; 


DEFENDERS HAVE SAID THE YALTA AGREEMENTS WERE SOUND. THAT THE TROUBLE 
CAME WHEN RUSSIA VIOLATED THEM. | 

THE STATE DEPARTMENT DISTRIBUTED THE TWO-VOLUME, 834-PAGE RECORD TO 
REPORTERS LATE THIS AFTERNOON, FOR PUBLICATION TONIGHT. 

THE ACTION CONCLUDED A LONG PERIOD OF UNCERTAINTY OVER WHETHER THE 
DOCUMENTS, VIRTUALLY ALL LABELED "TOP SECRET,* SHOULD BE GIVEN OUT, 

FVEN NOW THE FULL RECORD WAS NOT MADE PUBLIC. FOR EXAMPLE THERE 
UERE TWO DELETIONS IN PRIME MINISTER CHURCHILL'S REMARKS, IN WHICH HE 
WERE RENTLY REFERRED TO FRANCE'S POSTWAR ROLE» IT WAS ALSO REPORTED 
Art SOME COMMENT BY ROOSEVELT ON ANOTHER SUBJECT WAS STRICKEN OUT. 

MANY OF THE MILITARY PAPERS PREPARED BY STAFF AIDES SHOWED 
DELETIONS WHICH OFFICIALS SAID WERE MADE FOR SECURITY REASONS. IN 
SE TTION, THE STATE DEPARTMENT SAID THERE WERE A “LIMITED NUMBER OF 
APO SSIONS* TO AVOID "NEEDLESS OFFENSE" TO NATIONALITIES OR INDI 

SQ FAR AS THE RESULTS OF THE HISTORIC YALTA CONFERENCE ARE CON- 
sERNED THERE WAS LITTLE, IF ANYTHING, NEW IN THE PAPERS. THE AGREE- 
CERTS REACHED HAVE ALL BEEN MADE PUBLIC YEARS AGO. 

rs aT WAS NEW WERE DETAILS OF THE ARGUMENTS ROOSEVELT, CHURCHILL AND 

ain PRESENTED TO EACH OTHER, THE WAY THEY TALKED TO EACH OTHER, 

STAL INE MANEUVERINGS OF THREE LEADERS SHAPING THE FUTURE OF THE POsT- 
AN WORLD. IN THAT RESPECT THE PAPERS ARE A MINE FOR THE HISTORIAN AND 
ANALYST OF THE MOMENTOUS EVENTS» i 

\~ PAPERS NOTED THAT PRESIDENT ROOSEVELT SAID REBY 

THE PBTAINED TwO EXTRA VOTES IN THE U.N» WAS "VERY EMBARRASSING 
RUSSIA,OB TTS ARRANGEMENT WAS KEPT SECRET FOR A WHILE, BUT LATER BECAME 


KNOWN MOTHER POINT ROOSEVELT EXPRESSED THE HOPE THE BRITISH WOULD 
TURN THEIR GREAT PORT OF HONG KONG OVER TO CHINA--A HOPE THAT NEVER

EXPERIMENT AL 


SUB BELIEVED 
TO BE FASTEST 


Albacore May Become 
Pattern For Hulls Of 


Like Nuclear Craft 
ww &lt; 

| 

Washington, Marépi (P)—The! 

Navy for the last ygarfhas been 

testing an experimental  sub- 

marine which is believed to be 

faster than any other submersible 

afloat, for “sprint’’ distances un- 
der water. 





The submarine Albacore — a 
small, 1,300-ton craft with a shape 
something like an elongated tear- 
drop—may become the pattern 
for hulls of future nuclear en- 
gined submersibles. 

The Navy now has the atomic 
submarine Nautilus in operation 
and expects to launch a second, 
sister ship, the Sea Wolf, next 
month. Five others are to be built 
under current appropriations or 
requests for appropiations. 

The submerged speed of the 
Nautilus is officially reported to 
be over 20 knots. 

Probably The Fastest 

A navy spokesman, in answer 
to questions, said the Albacore 
“is faster than the Nautilus for 
short periods of time, probably 
the fastest submarine ever built.”’ 
But, he added, the Nautilus “has 
the fastest sustained speed of any 
submarine yet built.” 

He meant that the design of 








the hull of the Albacore makes 





possible high underwater speeu 
for short periods of time while 
using propulsion from storage 
batteries and the electric motor. 
But the battery power is ex- 
hausted in relatively short time 
by this full-power drain on the 
batteries. 

On the other hand, the Nautilus 
uses its main, atomic engine 
when submerged to provide 
steam for the turbine drive. It 
ean travel at full power on the 
main engine for days or even 
weeks, 

The Albacore was built at the 
Portsmouth (N.H.) navy yard 
and commissioned in December, 
1953. 

A Test Vehicle 

The boat is nearer to a true 
fishlike form than most sub- 
marines, with all cross-sections 
circular and its exterior smooth 
except for the narrow conning 
tower. The Albacore, being en- 
tirely a test vehicle for hull de- 
sign, carries no torpedo tubes or 
other armament. 

It is being used in the manner 
that the air industry studies aero- 
dynamic design development. 
Actually, a one-fifth size scale 
model of the Albacore had its 
first test in a wind tunnel] of the 
National Advisory Committee for 
Aeronautics, to detect drag and 
lift characteristics —as an _ air- 
plane model is tested for the 
Same purpose. 

The Navy says that on an equal 
volume basis, the hull form of the|: 
Albacore requires less than one 
half of the shaft horsepower of a 
standard guppy submarine to 
drive it at the same submerged 
eneed.

___ (ADVANCE) a aPARIS, MARCH 17 (AP)-A FRENCH MILITARY ENGINEER HAS COME 
UP WITH THE IDEA OF STORING THE ENERGY OF A HYDROGEN BOMB BY 

EXPLODING IT IN A HUGE ARTIFICIAL CAVERN FILLED WITH WATER 20,000 

FEET BELOW THE EARTH'S SURFACE. 

THE POWER OF THIS TAILOR-MADE VOLCANO COULD BE USED FOR BOTH 
DEFENSE AND INDUSTRIAL ENERGY, HE SAYS. 

CAMILLE ROUGERON HEADED THE ARMAMENTS SECTION AT THE FRENCH AIR 
MINISTRY BEFORE WORLD WAR II AND ACTED AS A TECHNICAL ADVISER TO THE 
WAR MINISTRY IMMEDIATELY AFTERWARDS. .NOW RETIRED, HE HAS WRITTEN FouR 
BOOKS. QN_WAR_AND HAS A NEW ONE COMING UP. SOME OF THE IDEAS IN IT Haver 
BEEN APPEARING IN L'AURORE. 

ROUGERON TOLD THE ASSOCIATED PRESS HE HAS EXPLAINED HIS 
SUGGESTIONS TO FRENCH AUTHORITIES INTERESTED IN CHEAP PRODUCTION OF 
POWER; THEIR REACTION IS *GENERALLY FAVORABLE.” 

THE FIRST DIFFICULTY IN HARNESSING THERMONUCLEAR ENERGY -- THE 
FORCE OF THE H-BOMB --IS THAT IT PRODUCES HEAT SO ENORMOUS AS TO 
VAPORIZE ANY PRACTICAL CONTAINER. ROUGERON'S IDEA OF A CONTAINER 
THEREFORE IS 20,000 FEET OF EARTH AND ROCKe HE CONSIDERS THAT WOtLp 
BE ENOUGH PROTECTION FOR AN "UNDERGROUND BOILER.”® WHERE H=BOMBS 
WOULD BE EXPLODED IN A CHAMBER HALF A MILE IN DIAMETER. 

FIRST A SHAFT WOULD HAVE TO BE SUNK WIDE ENOUGH TO ACCOMMODATE THE 
BOMBS. A CHEMICAL EXPLOSIVE AT THE BOTTOM OF THE SHAFT WOULD BLAST 
QUT A CHAMBER ABOUT 65 FEET IN DIAMETER. WATER WOULD THEN BE PUMPED 
INTO TH . 
A "SMALL® ATOMIC EXPLOSION AT THIS POINT, ROUGERON SAYS, WOULD: 
te ENLARGE THE CHAMBER ABOUT FOUR TIMES FOR THE HYDROGEN BLAST, 

2e PRODUCE STEAM THAT WOULD FLOW IINTO AN ELECTRICITY-GENERATING 
TURBINE AT THE SURFACE. 

WHEN WATER HAD BEEN PUMPED AGAIN INTO THE HOLE, EVERYTHING WOULD 
BE READY FOR THE BIG BLAST. 

A COMPARATIVELY *WEAK® HYDROGEN BOMB -- EQUIVALENT TO FIVE MILLION 
TONS OF TNT -- WOULD BLAST THE HALF MILE WIDE CHAMBER, ACCORDING 
TO ROUGERON. WHAT YOU WOULD HAVE THEN, HE SAYS, IS A GREAT STOCK OF 
STEAM FOR POWER AND RADIOACTIVE WATER FOR DEFENSE. HE SUGGESTED AN 
EXPLOSION IN THIS CHAMBER EVERY SIX MONTHS. 

HE SAYS THE HYDROGEN EXPLOSION COULD BE KEPT FROM COMING UP THE 
SHAFT BY PLUGGING IT WITH "SEVERAL HUNDRED YARDS" OF CONCRETE. HE 
ADDS THAT OTHER METHODS OF EASING THE EFFECT OF THE BLAST ARE ALSO 
KNOWN TO ENGINEERS. 

DRINKING WATER WOULD NOT BE AFFECTED, HE CONTENDS, BECAUSE THE 
HYDROGEN EXPLOSION WOULD SO COMPRESS THE WALLS OF THE CHAMBER AS TO ° 
MAKE THEM IMPERVIOUS TO RADIOACTIVITY. AND HE INSISTS THAT THE STEAM 
ITSELF WOULD NOT BE RADIOACTIVE -- ONLY THE SOLUTION OF WATER 
AND METALS REMAINING BELOW GROUND. |

POLITICAL ASYLUM BUT THAT IT WAS GRANTED ONLY TO KOLB.

STALIN'S STRATEGY FOR EXPANDING SOVIET POWER IN THE FAR EAST AND 
EUROPE WAS AIDED BY A LACK OF CLOSE COOPERATION BETWEEN PRESIDENT 
ROOSEVELT AND PRIME MINISTER CHURCHILL. 

ROOSEVELT WAS DOMINATED--THE RECORD INDICATES--BY TWIN DESIRES OF 
ASSURING (1) STALIN'S ENTRY INTO THE WAR AGAINST JAPAN AND (2) RUSSIA'S 
COOPERATION IN SETTING UP THE UNITED NATIONS« 

CHURCHILL WAS MORE RESISTANT TO STALIN'S DEMANDS AND PRIMARILY DEDI- 
CATED TO THE PROPOSITION OF PRESERVING THE BRITISH EMPIRE. 

IT IS IN FACT, THE UNDERLYING DRAMA OF THE FATE OF BRITAIN WHICH 
BREAKS THROUGH AT MANY POINTS OF THE YALTA PAPERS TO GIVE FRESH MEANING 
TO MANY EVENTS OF THE PAST DECADE AND TO THROW NEW LIGHT ON THE QUES- 
TION OF HOW THE WORLD GOT WHERE IT IS TODAY. 

IN ESSENCE, IN FEBRUARY, 1945, PRESIDENT ROOSEVELT APPEARED TO RE- 
GARD THE BRITISH EMPIRE AS’A CRUMBLING FORCE IN WORLD AFFAIRS AND TO 
ACCEPT THAT FACT WITH RESIGNATION IF NOT POSITIVE SATISFACTION, 

STALIN UNQUESTIONABLY STOOD TO PROFIT BY THE FALLING AWAY OF BRIT- 
ISH POWER IN KEY SPOTS LIKE THE EASTERN MEDITERRANEAN. 

ROOSEVELT--POSSIBLY MOTIVATED BY A DESIRE TO EXPAND THE AREA OF Po-

OF ITS WOMEN IN UNIFORM AGAINST WHAT IT CALLED A WIDESPREAD AND SOME- 
TIMES VICIOUS CAMPAIGN OF SLANDER IN WORLD WAR II.

CORPS (WAC) IS TOLD IN AN 800-PAGE VOLUME WHICH FORMS A PART OF THE 
ARMY'S OFFICIAL HISTORY OF WORLD WAR II.

STANDINGS AND THE DIFFICULTIES INTO WHICH THE WACS RAN HEADLONG.

LAS VEGAS, NEVey MARCH 23 (AP)-AN ATOMIC DEMOLITION DEVICE, ONE 
OF THE TINIEST YET DEVISED, WAS EXPLODED UNDERGROUMD ON YUCCA 
FLAT TODAY IN A SPECIAL TEST FOR THE ARMY'S CqRR ENGINEERS, 

THE AFTERNOON BLAST, SEVENTH OF THE SPRING &amp; AND SECOND IN 
TwO DAYS, SENT UP A VERTICAL STREAK OF FLAME BARELY VISIBLE ON A 
MOUNTAIN PEAK 55 MILES AWAYs 

ONLY A TRACE OF A FIREBALL WAS SEEN, BUT THE CLOUD PRODUCED was TuE 
DIRTIEST OF THE SERIES. DIRT SUCKED UP FROM THE DESERT FLOOR TURNED 
THE CLOUD ALMOST BROWN, EVEN EXTENDING INTO THE MINIATURE 
MUSHROOM WHICH ROSE ONLY TO 11,000 FEET. 

MOST OF THE DIRT FELL BACK ON THE SITE. THERE WAS NO_ REPETITION of 
YESTERDAY'S SCARE WHEN THE ATOMIC CLOUD SPRINKLED LIGHT RADIOACTIVITY 
FROM 40,000 FEET ON LAS VEGAS 

THE DEVICE ITSELF, PERHAPS LESS THAN ONE KILOTON IN POWER, WAS 
DESIGNED BYTHE LOS ALAMOS, Ne Mey LABORATORY OF THE ATOMIC ENERGY con- 
MISSION. A KILOTON IS EQUAL TO 1,000 TONS OF TNT. 

NEITHER THE AEC NOR ARMY DISCLOSED THE POTENTIAL WEAPON THE ENCI- 
NEERS ARE SEEKING TO PERFECT. 

TWENTY-SIX AIR FORCE PLANES PARTICIPATED IN THE TEST, INCLUDING A 
FLIGHT OF JETS SIMULATING A BOMB DELIVERY. 

THERE WERE NO TROOP MANEUVERS, BUT THE BLAST WAS VIEWED BY 280 
MILITARY OBSERVERS FROM A DISTANCE OF FIVE MILES. 

IT WAS THE FIRST UNDERGROUND TEST SINCE NOVEMBER, 1951, WHEN THE 
AEC HELD TWO TESTS DESCRIBED AMBIGUOUSLY AS "SURFACE OR GROUND" AT 
THE NEVADA SITE. 

THIS TIME, THE AEC CALLED ITS SHOT IN ADVANCE AND ARMY ENGINEERS 
AND ORDNANCE EXPERTS PLACED THE DEVICE IN THE HOLE. 
THE DEPTH WAS NOT DISCLOSED. 

THE BLAST WAS NOT FELT OR HEARD IN LAS VEGAS, 75 MILES AWAY. 

THREE HOURS LATER THERE WAS NO REPORTED FALLOUT OUTSIDE THE 
TEST SITE. YESTERDAY'S CLOUD DROPPED 174 MILLIROENTGENS OF RADIO- 
ACTI ITY ON NORTH LAS VEGAS, WELL BELOW THE FIGURE WHICH THE AEC 
REGARDS AS DANGEROUS.« 

TODAY'S TEST INVOLVED MILITARY AND CIVIL EFFECTS 
EXPERIMENTS BUT NO ANIMALS WERE USED,

ECONOMIC FRONT.

AND CAPITALISTIC SYSTEMS TO MEASURES SHORT OF WAR."

AS A MATTER OF FACT THE TIME FOR SOVIET 
THE WAR AGAINST JAPAN WAS AFTER THE JAPANESE ATTACK UpOM PEARLS 
HARBOR. AT THAT TIME THE: GERMAN ONSLAUGHT HAD BEEN STOPPED ON THE 
EASTERN FRONT AND A GREAT COUNTEROFFENSIVE OF THE SOVIET ARMIES WAS 
WELL UNDER WAY. HAD THE SOVIET THEN BROUGHT COMBAT PRESSURE ON 
JAPAN IN THE FAR EAST, JAPAN WOULD HAVE BEEN UNABLE TO CONDUCT 
OPERATIONS ON TWO FRONTS. HAD SHE BEEN ENGAGED IN THE NORTH, THE 
SOUTHERN FRONT IN ALL PROBABILITY NEVER WOULD HAVE BFEN OPENED. 

THIS WOULD -HAVE- SAVED THE -PHELEPPINES ,- MALAYA- AND- THE -DUTCH EAST 
INDIES AND PREVENTED THE JAPANESE THRUST OUT INTO THE PACIFIC TO THE 
VERY THRESHOLD OF AUSTRALIA. MILLIONS OF LIVES AND UNTOLD AGONIES 
WOULD HAVE BEEN SPARED BY SUCH A STRATEGIC COURSE WHICH I RECOMMENDED

DEC.13, 1941. I RECEIVED NO REPLY,

BY CARL HARTMAN “S55 
PARIS, MARCH 24 CAP)-TWO HALF-HEARTED SUPPORTERS OF THE PaRIS 

AGREEMENTS TO REARM WEST GERMANY CONTINUED THE RATIFICATION DEBATE 

IN THE FRENCH SENATEe OBSERVERS EXPECT THE UPPER HOUSE TO GIVE THE 

TREATIES FRANCE'S FINAL PARLIAMENTARY APPROVAL IN A VOTE LATE FRIDAY 

OR SATURDAY. 

YVON COUDE DU FORESTO, A MEMBER OF A CENTRIST PARTY, AND MARCEL 
CHAMPELX, A SOCIALIST, BOTH URGED THE UPPER-CHAMBER COUNCIL OF THE 
REPUBLIC, TO ACCEPT THE AGREEMENTS AS THE BEST THAT FRANCE CAN 
OBTAIN AT THIS TIME. 

ABOUT 40 OTHER SENATORS ARE LISTED TO SPEAK BEFORE THE FINAL 
VOTEe WHILE SOME HITCH IS ALWAYS POSSIBLE, THE OUTLOOK NOW IS THAT 
THE SENATE WILL ENDORSE THE ACCORDS. THEY HAVE ALREADY BEEN APPROVED 
RY THE NATIONAL ASSEMBLY, THE MORE POWERFUL BRANCH OF THE FRENCH 
LEGISLATUREs 

COUDE DU FORESTO SAID HE WOULD HAVE PREFERRED THE EUROPEAN ARMY 
(EDC) FORMULA FOR GERMAN REARMAMENT. BUT HE ADDED, "I BELIEVE WE 
MUST ACCEPT THE PARIS ACCORDS AS A LESSER EVIL," PREFERABLE TO 
ISOLATING FRANCE FROM HER ALLIES. 

CHAMPEIX SAID KE AND HIS SOCIALIST COLLEAGUES WERE GOING TO 
"SUBMIT® TO THE PARIS TREATIES RATHER THAN ®ACCEPT® THEM, EXPLAINING 
THAT THEY, TOO, WOULD HAVE PREFERRED THE EDC SOLUTION TO THE 
PROBLEMe 

HE CHIDED FORMER PREMIER PIERRE MENDES-FRANCE, SAYING THAT IF 
MENDES-FRANCE HAD EXPENDED ONLY A PART OF THE EFFORT TO GET EDC 
RATIFIED THAT HE HAD USED IN DRAWING UP THE PARIS ACCORDS, 

FRANCE WOULD HAVE ACCEPTED THE EUROPEAN ARMY PLAN. 

*THE PARIS TREATIES WERE NEITHER OUR GOAL NOR OUR IDEAL," CHAMPEIX 
SAID, BUT HE ADDED THAT FRANCE COULD NOT AFFORD TO REJECT THEM. 

MANY SENATORS, HOWEVER, SOUGHT ANOTHER POSTPONEMENT IN THE 
ALLIED PLANS TO REARM THE WEST GERMANS. THEY PINNED THEIR HOPES 
CHIEFLY ON AN AMENDMENT PROPOSED BY SEN. ANDRE ARMENGAUD, A MEMBER 
OF THE RIGHT-WING INDEPENDENTS.~ | 

HE WANTS TO PUT OPERATION OF THE TREATIES OFF UNTIL A SETTLEMENT 

IS REACHED ON THE WEST EUROPEAN ARMS POOL PROPOSED BY MENDES-FRANCE. 
OPPOSITION TO THE POOL IS STRONG IN WESTERN EUROPE, AND ARMENGAUD'S 
AMENDMENT WAS GIVEN SMALL CHANCE OF ADOPTION. ~

ION ABOUT THE EFFECTS OF NUCLEAR WEAPONS WHICH THE PUBLIC SHOULD KNOW 
FOR ITS OWN DEFENSE.

SapU PENNA, AUSTRIA, MARCH 25 (AP)-FEDERAL CHANCELLOR JULIUS RAAB

MOLOTOV YESTERDAY IN AN INTERVIEW WITH NORBERT BISCHOFF, AUSTRIA'S 
AMBASSADOR TO RUSSIA. THEIR MEETING WAS THE LATEST IN A RECENT 
SERIES OF EXCHANGES ON THE PACT, WHICH HAS BEEN DELAYED FOR 10 YEARS. 

(OFFICIALS IN WASHINGTON SUGGESTED THAT THE EXCHANGES WERE ANOTHER 

INRUSSIAN MANEUVER TO BLOCK GERMAN REARMAMENT.) 

THE TEXT OF THE INVITATION AS RELAYED BY BISCHOFF ARRIVED IN VIENNA 
LAST NIGHT AND IS NOW BEING STUDIED CLOSELY BY FOREIGN OFFICE OFFICIALS. 
IT WAS LEARNED THAT THE GOVERNMENT'S OFFICIAL REPLY PROBABLY WILL 
NOT BE MADE PUBLIC BEFORE NEXT WEEK. 

THE AUSTRIAN CABINET HAS RECALLED ITS AMBASSADORS IN WASHINGTON, 
LONDON, PARIS AND MOSCOW, FOR CONSULTATIONS. THEY ARE SCHEDULED TO 
ARRIVE HERE NEXT MONDAY. 

A TOP GERMAN OFFICIAL MEANWHILE DISPUTED MOLOTOV'S SUGGESTION THAT 
THERE WAS DANGER OF ANOTHER UNION BETWEEN GERMANY AND AUSTRIA. 

SPEAKING IN LONDON WHERE HE IS HOLDING TALKS WITH BRITISH FOREIGN 
SECRETARY SIR ANTHONY EDEN, HEINRICH VON BRETANO SAID INAN INTERVIEW 
THAT THE ADENAUER GOVERNMENT WAS OPPOSED TO SUCH A UNION “NOW AND AT 
ANY TIME I N THE FUTURE." VON BRETANO IS PARLIAMENTARY LEADER OF 
ADENAUER'S RULING CHRISTIAN DEMOCRAT PARTY. _

STOCKHOLM, SWEDEN, MARCH 26 (AP)-SOVIET PREMIER BU i" 
REMARKS ABOUT A BIG FOUR CONFERENCE SPARKED NEW SPECULATION TONIGHT 
THAT ANDREI GROMYKO IS HERE TO LINE UP STOCKHOLM AS A SITE. 

RELIABLE INFORMANTS SAID THE SOVIET FIRST DEPUTY FOREIGN MINISTER 
HAS NOT YET BROUGHT UP THE SUBJECT IN TALKS WITH HIGH SWEDISH 
OFFICIALS, INCLUDING KING GUSTAF VI AND PREMIER TAGE ERLANDER. 

ASKED ABOUT SUCH REPORTS, GROMYKO REPLIED$ "I CAN SAY NOTHING YET." 

WESTERN DIPLOMATS BEL{EVE ANY BIG FOUR CONFERENCE WOULD BE HELD IN 
A NEUTRAL COUNTRY. THERE WAS A REPORT THAT PRIME MINISTER CHURCHILL 
ONCE SUGGESTED STOCKHOLM AS THE SPOT FOR A FOUR-POWER MEETING.

HIS WAY TO BE CORDIAL. HE DOES NOT PLAN TO LEAVE FOR MOSCOW UNTIL

THEY HAD NOTHING TO DISCUSS WITH HIM AT A HIGH DIPLOMATIC LEVEL.

TOKYO, SUNDAY, MARCH 27 (AP)-JAPAN'S ENTHUSIASM FOR TRADE WITH 
RED CHINA HAS TAKEN A NOSE DIVE, KYODO NEWS SERVICE SAID TODAY, 

THIS REPORT BY JAPAN'S ONLY MAJOR NEWS SERVICE CAME JUST A FEW 
HOURS AFTER THE ARRIVAL HERE OF SIX MEMBERS OF A RED CHINA TRADE 

PRIME MINISTER ICHIRO HATOYAMA, BOTH BEFORE AND AFTER THE RECENT 
JAPANESE ELECTIONS, STRESSED INCREASED TRADE WITH RED CHINA. BUT HIs 
GOVERNMENT HAS SAID JAPAN WILL NOT EXPORT STRATEGIC ITEMS BANNED BY 
THE WESTERN NATIONS COORDINATING COMMITTEE FOR EXPORT CONTROL. 

KYODO SAID JAPAN'S HEAVY AND STRATEGIC MATERIALS INDUSTRIES ARE 
NOT INTERESTED IN NEGOTIATING WITH THE RED CHINA TRADE MISSION UNTIL 
THE BAN IS LIFTED. MANY JAPANESE BELIEVE RED CHINA TRADE WILL 
NOT AMOUNT TO MUCH FOR SEVERAL YEARS AND THEY DO NOT WANT TO 
ENDANGER THEIR FREE WORLD CONTACTS BY SUCH TRADE. 

THE NEWS SERVICE SAID IT HAD MADE A SURVEY WHICH SHOWED MAJOR 
BUSINESS AND INDUSTRIAL LEADERS WOULD AVOID CONTACT WITH THE TRADE

GROUP AND COUNTER-ATTACK BEFORE HE FELL.

ESSEN, GERMANY, MARCH 27 (AP)-ALFRIED KRUPP SAID TODAY HIS - 
INDUSTRIAL CONCERN, BARRED BY THE CONQUERING ALLIES FROM PRODUCING 
COAL AND STEEL, HAS REGAINED A FIRM HOLD IN THE WORLD MARKET AND IS 
FXPANDING ITS INTERNATIONAL OPERATIONS. 
~ THE 46-YEAR-OLD HEIR..QF_ THE. FORMER GERMAN ARMAMENT EMPIRE ALSO TOLD 
VETERAN WORKERS THAT "AS A RESULT OF ALLIED CONTROLS AND RESTRICTIONS, 
THE HOUSE OF KRUPP IS MOVING INTO NEW FIELDS (OF PRODUCTION) ON A 
GLOBAL SCALE." 

KRUPP SAID HIS FIRM WAS PARTICIPATING IN BIG INDUSTRIAL PROJECTS 
IN ASIA, EUROPE AND SOUTH AMERICA. DOMESTICALLY, HE ANNOUNCED, HE IS 
GETTING INTO PLASTICS. x 5 

HE DISCLOSED THAT INDIA HAS APPROVED PROPOSALS FOR CONSTRUCTION BY 
HIS COMPANY OF A COMPLETE INDUSTRIAL CITY OF 100,000 FOR STEEL WORKERS 
AND THEIR FAMILIES. THE STEEL WORKERS WILL BE EMPLOYED IN THE INDIAN 
ROURKELA STEEL MILL WHICH, WITH A PLANNED CAPACITY OF A MILLION TONS, 
WILL ALSO BE CONSTRUCTED BY KRUPP IN COOPERATION WITH THE DEMAG (ALL 


CAPS) MACHINERY PLANT IN DUISBURG. 

KRUPP SPOKE DURING THE COMPANY'S ANNUAL JUBILEE CEREMONIES AT THE 
VILLA HUEGEL, FORMER KRUPP FAMILY RESIDENCE. REPORTERS WERE BARRED 
BUT EXCERPTS OF HIS SPEECH WERE MADE AVAILABLE TO THEM. 

WITH REGARD TO PLASTICS, KRUPP COMMENTED HE HAS BOUGHT AN AMERICAN 
LICENSE FOR "NEW TYPES OF MACHINERY FOR PRODUCTION OF SYNTHETIC 
FIBRES.®

METHODS--WHICH ARE OUT OF DATE TODAY--MUST BE DROPPED FROM OUR ;

USE OF ATOMIC EXPLOSION WILL INVOLVE A DIFFERENT PRINCIPLE THAN 
THAT OF CONVENTIONAL ANTIAIRCRAFT FIRE. THE KNOCK-DOWN OF AIRCRAFT 
BY ATOMIC WEAPONS WILL DEPEND ALMOST ENTIRELY ON THE DESTRUCTIVE 
SHOCK WAVE OF THE EXPLOSION. WITH CONVENTIONAL *FLAK" MOST OF THE 
DAMAGE RESULTS FROM FRAGMENTATION OF THE SHELL CASING. THIS IS 


PARTICULARLY TRUE OF EXPLOSIONS BY PROXIMITY-FUSED SHELLS WHERE THERE 
IS NO ACTUAL CONTACT WITH THE AIRCRAFT TO PRODUCE DETONATION.

THE INFORMANTS SAID AN AMERICAN-BRITISH=FRENCH COMMITTEE OF 
EXPERTS IS LIKELY TO BE SET UP IN LONDON OR PARIS TO STUDY THE MANY 
COMPLICATED PROBLEMS CONNECTED WITH THE PROJECT TO MEET WITH RUSSIA. 
ITS TASK WILL BE TO CLEAR THE GROUND AND COORDINATE POLICIES IN LINE

THE THREE-POWER STUDY GROUP MAY BROADEN ITS DIRECTIVES WHEN THE

OFFICIALS MIGHT COME IN WHEN THEIR COUNTRY IS UNDER DISCUSSION.

THAT BROUGHT OUT THE PROPOSAL IN MARCH 1953 AND HAD INTRODUCED 
THE SEPTEMBER 1951 RESOLUTION BY WHICH THE COUNCIL SET UP THE 
COMMITTEE. THE SWITCH IN POLICY FOLLOWS A CHANGE IN ADMINISTRATION. 
THE SO CALLED "AD HOC COMMITTEE ON RESTRICTIVE BUSINESS PRACTICES” 
WAS TO PROPOSE METHODS TO BE ADOPTED BY INTERNATIONAL AGREEMENT TO 
PREVENT HARMFUL PRACTICES RESTRAINING COMPETITION, LIMITING ACCESS TO 
MARKETS OR FOSTERING MONOPOLISTIC CONTROL. IT WORKED FROM A CHAPTER OF 
THE HAVANA TRADE CHARTER OF 1948 THAT HAS NEVER GONE INTO FORCE. 
THE U.S. NOTE SAID GOVERNMENTS DIFFERED SO WIDELY AMONG

LONDON, MARCH 29 (AP)-THE COMMUNIST NEW CHINA NEWS AGENCY CHARGED 
TODAY THAT LAOS GOVERNMENT TROOPS ATTACKED ANTI-ROYALIST UNITS 
IN THE MUONG PEUNG AREA OF INDOCHINA AND PLUNDERED VILLAGES.

ANTI-ROYALISTS -- KNOWN AS PATHET-LAO -- FOUGHT BACK AND FORCED 
THE ATTACKERS TO WITHDRAW. IT ADDED THAT A SECOND ATTACK THE SAME 
DAY, MARCH 24, WAS ALSO FOUGHT OFF. 

tHE LAOS KINGDOM IS ONE OF THE THREE INDOCHINA STATES ASSOCIATED 
WITH THE FRENCH UNION. LAST YEAR'S GENEVA AGREEMENT ON INDOCHINA 
CALLED FOR BOTH SIDES TO REACH A SETTLEMENT, BUT TALKS HAVE 
DEADLOCKED AND LOCAL CLASHES CONTINUE.

TOKYO, MARCH 30 CAP)-THE PHILIPPINES TODAY WARNED ASIAN 
NATIONS THAT TRADING WITH COMMUNIST CHINA WOULD STRENGTHEN THE 
REDS ABILITY TO "COMMIT FURTHER AGGRESSIONS IN THIS REGION.” 

DRe PERFECTO LAGUIO, CHIEF PHILIPPINE DELEGATE, TOLD THE_U.N.} 
ECONOMIC COMMISSION FOR ASIA AND THE FAR EAST CECAFE) THAT THE 
PHILIPPINES GOVERNMENT WAS FIRMLY AGAINST TRADE WITH THE REDS.» 

DRe LAGUIO CITED THREE REASONS? 


—_— 


1. "THE UNITED NATIONS HAS AN EMBARGO ON TRADE WITH THAT ee 
(RED CHINA), PARTICULARLY ON STRATEGIC MATERIALS." wie edy 

2. "WHILE OUR GOVERNMENT RECOGNIZES THAT SOME OTHER MEMBER GOVERN- 
MENTS QF ECAFE HAVE TOLERATED SOME (RED CHINA) TRADE IN NON-STRATEG Ic 
COMMODITIES, IT IS THE FEELING OF MY GOVERNMENT THAT SUCH TRADE WOULD 
SERVE TO STRENGTHEN THE ECONOMY OF RED CHINA AND THUS ENABLE HER TO 
COMMIT FURTHER AGGRESSIONS IN THIS REGION." 

3. “THE PHILIPPINE ECONOMY COULD CONTINUE UNIMPAIRED AND SO 
COULD MANY OF THE ECONOMIES OF OTHER SOVEREIGN STATES IN THE ECAFE 
REGION WITHOUT TRADING WITH RED CHINA." 

ANY TRADING WITH COMMUNIST CHINA, DR.» LAGUIO ASSERTED, “WILL ONLY 

THEREBY ENDANGER PEACE AND TRAN- 


STRENGTHEN AN AGGRESSOR NATION AND 
QUILITY IN THE ECAFE REGION."

"AGGRESSIVE MILITARISTIC POLICIES."

THE RESULT OF OUTSIDE INTERFERENCE. 

*NOTHING COULD BE FURTHER FROM THE TRUTH.

ARE PURELY VOLUNTARY. WE DO, OF COURSE, TAKE INTO CONSIDERATION OUR 
TOTAL RELATIONS WITH ALL FRIENDLY COUNTRIES OF THE FREE WORLD."

LEBANON, MARCH 31 CAP)-A CZECH DIPLOMAT SEEKING POLITICAL 
RITAIN WITH HIS FAMILY LEFT BEIRUT BY DUTCH AIRLINER 

SECOND TIME. BAD WEATHER HAD FORCED THE PLANE BACK LAST 
NIGHT. = 


THE REFUGEE, RICHARD SEDLACEK, 38, HAD BEEN COMMUNIST 
CZECHOSLOVAKIA'S COMMERCIAL ATTACHE IN DAMASCUS, SYRIA. HE CAME 
TO BEIRUT EARLIER THIS WEEK WITH HIS WIFE HELENA, AND THEIR FIVE- 
YEAR-OLD SON RICHARD. 

SEDLACEK TOLD NEWSMEN LAST NIGHT THE BRITISH HAD GIVEN HIM A visa 
FOR A FEW MONTHS BUT HAD NOT RULED ON HIS REQUEST FOR ASYLUM. 

THE CZECH SAID HIS COUNTRY IS INCREASINGLY BECOMING A SOVIET 
COLONY AND HE WANTS HIS SON RICHARD TO "GROW UP IN AN ATMOSPHERE oF 
FREEDOM AND GET A CHRISTIAN EDUCATION." 

SEDLACEK TOLD NEWSMEN HE CAME TO THE CZECH LEGATION IN BEIRUT IN 
APRIL, 1952, AND LAST YEAR WAS SENT TO DAMASCUS. RECENTLY HE WAS 
ORDERED TO RETURN TO CZECHOSLOVAKIA, "BUT IF I HAD GONE HOME I WOULD 
HAVE HAD TO SEND MY SON TO SCHOOL THERE AND HE WOULD BEEN OBLIGED To 
REMAIN THERE ALWAYS." 

SEDLACEK SAID HE WAS LAST IN CZECHOSLOVAKIA IN APRIL AND MAY, 1953, 

“AT THAT TIME, WORKERS AND FARMERS WERESTRONGLY OPPOSED TO THE 
COMMUNIST REGIME," HE SAID. ; . hi 

THE CZECH SAID MANY OF HIS COLLEAGUES JN BEIRUT AND DAMASCUS WOULD 
LIKE TO FLEE TO THE WEST, BUT DO NOT BECAUSE "THEY HAVE RELATIVES 
INSIDE CZECHOSLOVAKIA AND SO DO NOT DARE TO ESCAPE BECAUSE OF FEAR 
OF REPRISALS." CZECH FOREIGN POLICY, HE ADDED, “IN GENERAL IS 
DIRECTED BY THE SOVIETS."

ANKARA, TURKEY, MARCH 31 (AP)-THE GOVERNMENT SAID TODAY 
MILITARY MISSIONS WILL ARRIVE HERE TOMORROW'FROM IRAQ AND JORDAN, 

THE VISITS, AT TURKEY'S INVITATION, COINCIDED WITH A PERIOD 
OF STRAINED RELATIONS BETWEEN THIS COUNTRY AND NEIGHBOR SYRIA. 

ANKARA OBJECTS STRONGLY TO A PROPOSED DEFENSE ALLIANCE OF SYRIA, 
EGYPT, AND SAUDI ARABIA WHICH WOULD EXCLUDE NON-ARAB MEMBERS. 

THE TURKS MAINTAIN THIS NEW GROUPING IS AIMED AT THEM. AN OFFICIAl 
SOURCE SAID EARLIER TODAY THE TURKISH ARMY HAS ORDERED TWO ARMORED 
BRIGADES TOTALLING ABOUT 10,000 MEN INTO THE AREA BORDERING SYRIA AND 
WILL SEND A THIRD BRIGADE THERE SOON. 

FRICTION BETWEEN THE ANKARA AND DAMASCUS GOVERNMENTS STARTED WITH 
THE SIGNING OF A TURKISH-IRAQI DEFENSE PACT. IRAQ IS A MEMBER OF THE 
ARAB LEAGUE; TURKEY IS NOT. EGYPT, SYRIA, AND SAUDI ARABIA OBJECTED 
TO ANY ALLIANCE BETWEEN LEAGUE MEMBERS AND OUTSIDERS. 

THE IRAQI AND JORDAN MILITARY MISSIONS WILL JOIN SIMILAR MISSIONS 
FROM LEBANON AND IRAN IN REVIEWING A BIG MILITARY PARADE HERE 


SUNDAY.

SYRIAN GOVERNMENT MOSCOW SUPPORTS SYRIAN ATTITUDE "IN THE FACE OF 
TURKISH PRESSURE.”

PEIPING HAS CRITIZED HONG KONG OFTEN. THERE HAVE BEEN BLOODY

Bi CAUSED SOME PEOPLE HERE--NOTABLY TRADERS WHOSE TRAFFIC HAD ALWAYS BEEN 
Fi WITH CHINA--TO TAKE A PATH OF CONCILIATION TOWARDS THE REDS. THERE 
ARE OTHERS HERE WHO ARE MORE AFRAID OF COMMUNIST INDULGENCE. THEY SAY 
M THE COMMUNISTS MAY BEHAVE WITH POLITICAL CORRECTNESS FOR YEARS, THEN 
R cUDDENLY TRUMP UP A GRIEVANCE AND STRIKE WITHOUT WARNING. 
SHIPS, YARDS, WAREHOUSES, DOCKS AND BANKS MAKE THIS PLACE ONE 
of THE WORLD'S GREAT PORTS AND MONEY CENTERS. THE MAN WHO MOST 
CLANTS THE BRITISH TO HOLD ON HERE IS THE REFUGEE FROM CHINA-- 
AND THERE ARE AT LEAST A MILLION OF HIM. HE MIGHT LOSE HIS NECK 
$F THE REDS CAME. 
i HONG KONG IS THE END OF THE LINE FOR HIM--HE HAS NO PASSPORT 
L THAT WILL GET HIM_ANY FARTHER. HE LIVES A HARD LIFE HERE, BUT AT 
FAST HE LIVES. HE MAY NOT, IN THE ABSTRACT, LIKE COLONIALISM, 
{bit BRITISH COLONIALISM IN’THIS PATCH OF EARTH HAS GIVEN HIP

'aTTACK BECAUSE THE COLONY WAS MORE USEFUL TO THE REDS IN BRITISH 
(HANDSe IT IS A FREE PORT WITH WORLD TRADE CONNECTIONS. THE REDS 
KEEP SCORES OF TRADE AGENTS HERE WHO PLACE ORDERS, ARRANGE 
SHIPPING, AND SELL EXPORTS, ALL RIGHT IN HONG KONG. NOT MUCH 
OF THE CARGO COMES HERE BUT IT IS ORDERED, BOUGHT OR SOLD FROM HERE 
THIS SAVES THE EXPENSE OF KEEPING AGENTS ALL OVER THE WORLD. SINCE 
THE START OF THE WEST'S EMBARGO ON SENDING STRATEGIC GOODS TO. 
RED CHINA HONG KONG'S VALUE AS A CONVENIENT BUYING AND SELLING 
BASE HAS SHRUNK. | 
MANY AMERICANS FEEL THAT HONG KONG IS TOO ANXIOUS TO DO BUSINESS 


WITH THE REDSe BUT FOR EVERY APPEASING TRADER THERE ARE THOUSANDS HERE HIMSE
